package_info.package_manager: custom (delivered via ZIP, not public package repository)
package_info.package_versions: unknown (malware distributed as ZIP payload, not versioned)
package_info.why_malicious: SnailResin is a custom malware distributed via spear-phishing and fake job recruitment lures, designed for cyber espionage. It is delivered as a disguised ZIP file, uses obfuscation and custom code to evade detection, and exfiltrates sensitive information from targeted systems. The malware leverages legitimate services for command and control, and its behavior is entirely inconsistent with any legitimate software package.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user opens malicious attachment or executes payload)
execution_context.file_location: malicious executable or DLL inside ZIP archive (e.g., SnailResin.exe or side-loaded DLL)

malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely C++/C#/Python, actual code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects system and environment information, enumerates files, and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled domains via HTTP(S), enabling espionage and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive information and sends it to external domains controlled by the attacker, which is a hallmark of espionage malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate job application documents or executables should not collect system information or communicate with external C2 servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise inventory or remote support tools may collect system info, but only with user consent and to trusted domains.
key_indicators: Collection of system and environment data without user consent
Network communication to attacker infrastructure (careers2find.com, xboxapicenter.com)
Execution triggered by opening a job-related attachment

execution_context.file_location: malicious DLL placed alongside legitimate application (DLL side-loading vector)

malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely C++/C#, actual code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the DLL is loaded by a legitimate application, the code decrypts and executes a malicious payload, establishes persistence, and communicates with attacker-controlled infrastructure via GitHub or similar services.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading is a common malware technique to evade detection by abusing trusted applications. The use of GitHub for C2 is also highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs should not decrypt and execute hidden payloads or establish unauthorized persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software may update itself via GitHub, but not via hidden payloads in side-loaded DLLs.
key_indicators: Decryption and execution of hidden payloads
C2 communication via public code hosting (GitHub)

attack_chain.action: Victim receives spear-phishing email with a ZIP attachment disguised as a job-related document.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens ZIP and executes malicious file

attack_chain.action: Victim opens the ZIP file and executes the malicious executable or triggers DLL side-loading.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware collects system information and establishes C2

attack_chain.action: Malware collects system and environment information, enumerates files, and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled domains.
Malware establishes persistence and maintains communication with C2 via legitimate services (e.g., GitHub, Cloudflare).

behavioral_signatures: Execution of unknown binaries or DLLs from ZIP attachments received via email
Collection of system and environment information immediately after execution
Network communication to attacker-controlled domains (careers2find.com, xboxapicenter.com, raw.githubusercontent.com/msdnedgesupport)
DLL side-loading by legitimate applications with subsequent network activity
file_indicators: ZIP attachments containing executables or DLLs with job-related filenames
Malicious DLLs placed alongside legitimate applications (side-loading vector)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of unknown binaries or DLLs originating from ZIP attachments, especially those received via email with job-related lures. Detect DLL side-loading activity by monitoring for unexpected DLLs loaded by trusted applications. Alert on outbound network connections to known attacker infrastructure (careers2find.com, xboxapicenter.com, raw.githubusercontent.com/msdnedgesupport, and related IPs). Correlate file hashes and filenames with known indicators of compromise. Use endpoint detection to flag collection of system/environment data and suspicious persistence mechanisms.
